summary: binding.gyp abuses node-gyp command execution to exfiltrate environment and filesystem data to webhook.site
details: The package ships a binding.gyp with a type:'none' target and no native C/C++ sources. Its action field invokes `node -e` with an inline payload that executes automatically during `node-gyp rebuild` (triggered implicitly by npm when gypfile:true), with no declared lifecycle scripts needed. The payload enumerates process.env in full (Object.keys(process.env) + key=value serialization), greps installer filesystem paths including /workspace/, /root/, /tmp/, /opt/, /var/, and /etc/ for an 'HTB{' token, reads /tmp/scent-trail.jsonl and /workspace/repo/package.json, and POSTs the collected data to https://webhook.site/f604623f-fc78-4447-9225-6772f7f12cb1. The binding.gyp is the entire attack surface — no native build is actually performed, the file exists solely to smuggle execution into the install step. The version string 99999.0.0 is implausibly high and consistent with a dependency-confusion win against an internal package name.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
